title: Local Bounti Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Highlights Pending Acquisition of Revol Greens' Certified Organic Greenhouse Facilities in Texas and Minnesota

*Pending Acquisition Expected to Add 30 Acres of Operating, Certified Organic Greenhouse Capacity, the Revol Brand, and Expansion Into the Midwest*


*Local Bounti to Become Largest Leafy Greens Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) Grower in the U.S. by Greenhouse Acreage, With Growing Footprint Set to Expand by 70% Upon Closing*


*FoodVentures, a Member of the DENSO Group, Local Bounti's Existing Strategic Investor and Other Investors Back Pending Transaction*


*Third Quarter Net Loss Improved 36% Year-over-Year; Year-to-Date Sales Up 10% to $39.6 Million*


HAMILTON, Mont.


, Nov. 23, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- Local Bounti Corporation (NYSE: LOCL) ("Local Bounti" or the "Company"), a breakthrough U.S. indoor agriculture company currently servicing approximately 13,000 retail doors, today reported its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided an update on its agreement to acquire the Texas and Minnesota greenhouse facilities and brand of Revol Greens, which is expected to close in the coming days.


Kathleen Valiasek, President and CEO of Local Bounti, stated, "Our pending acquisition of Revol Greens' facilities in Texas and Minnesota is an important step for Local Bounti. We are excited to welcome the Revol Greens team, and upon closing, together we will be the largest leafy greens CEA grower in the U.S. Demand for our products is outpacing our capacity, so every time we need to add capacity, we weigh building against buying, and in this case, buying was the clear choice: we are adding 30 acres of certified-organic greenhouse capacity that is already growing and selling to retailers, along with a brand that retailers and consumers in these markets know and trust. Just as important is who is backing this transaction: FoodVentures (part of the DENSO Group), our existing strategic investor, and other long-term investors who understand the same opportunity we see in CEA. At a time when capital in our industry is scarce, sophisticated long-term investors are choosing those operators with flexible formats that can evolve to meet growing consumer needs in both quality and safety."


Turning to the quarter, Ms. Valiasek continued, "The third quarter was a difficult one for our industry. Many consumers stopped buying lettuce and salads after the Cyclospora outbreak, which was tied to outdoor conventional growers. Our products were not involved because of our indoor growing approach. Although the outbreak came at a cost, it has put food safety and traceability at the center of our conversations with retailers, which is exactly why we founded Local Bounti: to give retailers and consumers confidence in the safety and traceability of their produce by growing it in controlled indoor environments. That is what our model was built for, and those conversations are turning into new business, including two new retail partners - Albertsons in Denver across approximately 110 stores serving the Rocky Mountain region and Brookshire Brothers across approximately 66 stores in the Mid-South, and an expansion with WinCo Foods, an existing customer, into Texas, bringing our baby leaf line to approximately 91 of their stores."


**Recent Developments: Pending Acquisition of Revol Greens' Facilities**


On November 16, 2026, Local Bounti entered into an agreement to acquire two certified-organic controlled environment agriculture (CEA) facilities in Texas (20 acres) and Minnesota (10 acres) from Revol Greens, along with the Revol brand and related intellectual property, for total consideration of approximately $19.6 million. The acquisition is expected to close in the coming days, after the end of the third quarter, and accordingly the Company's third quarter results and September 30, 2026 balance sheet do not reflect the facility assets to be acquired or the related financing.


Upon closing, with the 20 acre Texas facility and the 10 acre Minnesota facility, Local Bounti's growing footprint is expected to increase by roughly 70%, which would make it the largest leafy greens CEA grower in the U.S. as measured by greenhouse acreage. The Minnesota facility will extend the Company's growing and distribution network into the Midwest, where Revol Greens has built strong, trusted relationships with retail customers, and the Texas facility will strengthen its existing presence in the Southern U.S.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Summary**


- The Cyclospora outbreak weighed on demand for lettuce and salad products across the industry in the third quarter; according to Circana, U.S. retail produce sales were down $683 million year-over-year from July 19 to August 23, 2026. Against that backdrop, Local Bounti's sales increased 1% to $12.4 million, as compared to $12.2 million in the prior year period, as growth at the Georgia, Texas, and Washington facilities more than offset the lower demand due to Cyclospora.
- Net loss decreased to $17.0 million in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to net loss of $26.4 million for the prior year period, primarily due to a $3.7 million improvement in loss from operations driven by lower operating expenses, partially offset by lower gross profit, and a $5.6 million favorable change in the fair value of warrant liabilities, reflecting a $2.2 million gain in the current period as compared to a $3.4 million loss in the prior year period.
- Adjusted EBITDA1 loss improved to $6.2 million in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to a loss of $7.2 million in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA loss for the third quarter of 2026 excludes $1.2 million in stock-based compensation, $4.7 million in interest expense, $5.6 million of depreciation and amortization, a $2.2 million gain on change in fair value of warrant liability, and other non-core items.


1See the reconciliation of GAAP measures to non-GAAP measures at the end of this press release for more information.


**Food Safety**


Retailers, customers, and consumers continue to pay close attention to the safety and traceability of fresh produce, and to where and how it is grown. The recent Cyclospora outbreak, which public health authorities linked to conventional field-grown lettuce, has put those questions in sharper focus. Conversations with retailers now increasingly center on traceability, water sourcing, and environmental control. Local Bounti expects this focus to support long-term growth as retailers and consumers alike increasingly choose products based on the brand and on where and how those products are grown.


In August 2026, the Company's Mount Pleasant, Texas facility scored 100% on an unannounced food safety audit, and in October 2026, the Company scored 98% on the annual food safety audits of its two California facilities. The Texas and Minnesota facilities to be acquired each also scored 100% on their most recent food safety audits.


**Distribution**


Local Bounti currently services approximately 13,000 retail doors across 35 U.S. states and continues to build on its base of blue-chip retail relationships. Recent distribution highlights include:


- In the first and second quarters of 2026, the Company was awarded bids extending supply arrangements with multiple national retail accounts, spanning key product lines including baby leaf lettuce and organic butter lettuce.
- In the third quarter of 2026, the Company was again awarded bids extending supply agreements for its butterhead lettuce from its California and Texas facilities with a national retail account through the second quarter of 2028.
- In July 2026, the Company launched a new retail partner, Brookshire Brothers, in the Mid-South region featuring five SKUs across approximately 66 retail stores.
- In August 2026, the Company launched a new retail partner in the Rocky Mountain region, Albertsons' Denver division, featuring four SKUs across approximately 110 stores, with shipments beginning early in the month.
- In August 2026, the Company added distribution of its cress to approximately 134 stores in the Northern California region with an existing retail partner.
- In August 2026, the Company added approximately 97 US Foods CHEF'STORE locations, now carrying butterhead lettuce from its California facilities and serving the western half of the U.S.
- In September 2026, the Company expanded its partnership with WinCo Foods, an existing Western U.S. grocery retailer, adding a fifth baby leaf SKU across approximately 77 stores in Idaho and Oregon and, for the first time, launching four baby leaf SKUs across approximately 14 stores in Texas, both beginning in October 2026. This brings the Company's baby leaf distribution with this partner to approximately 91 stores, building on the launch of its living butter lettuce in the partner's Texas stores earlier this year.


Together, these wins reflect the strength of the Company's relationships with blue-chip retail partners and their continued confidence in Local Bounti's ability to deliver consistent, high-quality products over the long term. The pending acquisition of Revol Greens is expected to build on this foundation, adding a certified-organic offering and established retail relationships in the Midwest, so retail partners will be able to source a broader assortment, including organic, from a single grower.


**Commercial Facilities Update**


*Packaging Efficiency and Scalability*


The Texas Revol facility to be acquired features a top-of-the-line packaging room and fully automated equipment capable of packing all of Local Bounti's current baby leaf retail SKUs, as well as foodservice and bulk product. The packhouse is also equipped for head lettuce packaging and to create custom blends and mixes that can serve as customer exclusives or market differentiators. Built for growth, it can pack the facility's full 20 acres of greenhouse capacity in a single shift and has room to scale to more than 40 acres with no new construction.


*Cost Reduction Initiatives*


Across all facilities, the Company continues to make tangible progress on the cost side of the business. Year-to-date, salaries, benefits, and payroll-related expenses within general and administrative expense declined $1.7 million versus the prior year period, and more efficient seeding practices lowered seed costs by approximately 20% year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026. The Company expects to continue garnering cost savings across procurement, maintenance, labor efficiency, and freight management across the network.


**Capital Structure**


The Company ended the quarter with cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash of $11.9 million as of September 30, 2026.


In August 2026, the Company received an additional $12.5 million investment, in the form of a convertible note and common stock purchase warrant, from an existing strategic investor, further demonstrating continued confidence in Local Bounti's business and long-term growth trajectory. This amount is reflected in the Company's September 30, 2026 cash balance. The investment follows the $15 million investment received from the existing strategic investor in March 2026 and the transactions the Company executed in 2025.


As of September 30, 2026, Local Bounti had approximately 23.6 million shares outstanding, 13.3 million common shares under warrants outstanding, and approximately 2.4 million restricted stock units outstanding. The Company also has out-of-the-money convertible notes that, if converted, would result in the issuance of approximately 19.7 million common shares. Including the shares issuable in the event of conversion of the convertible notes, as well as the warrants and restricted stock units, the Company had a fully diluted share count of approximately 59.0 million shares outstanding as of September 30, 2026.


**Financial Outlook**


The Company remains focused on growing distribution with blue-chip retail partners, reducing costs, and integrating the Revol Greens facilities once acquired, and achieving positive adjusted EBITDA remains a key priority. Additional capacity at the Texas facility to be acquired is expected to support growth as that capacity becomes sold out. Fourth quarter 2026 results will include transaction and integration costs related to the acquisition.


**Conference Call**


The Company will host a conference call with members of the Local Bounti executive management team. The conference call is scheduled to begin at 4:30 p.m. ET on Monday, November 23, 2026. To participate on the live call, Listeners in North America may dial (877) 514-3624 and international listeners may dial +1 (201) 689-8883; the passcode is 13762893.


In addition, the call will be broadcast live via webcast, hosted at the "Investors" section of the Company's website at localbounti.com and will be archived online.


**About Local Bounti**


Local Bounti is redefining indoor farming with an innovative method – its patented Stack & Flow Technology® – that significantly improves crop turns, increases output and improves unit economics. Local Bounti operates advanced indoor growing facilities across the United States, servicing approximately 13,000 retail doors. Local Bounti grows healthy food utilizing a hybrid approach that integrates the best attributes of controlled environment agriculture with natural elements. Local Bounti's sustainable growing methods are better for the planet, using 90% less land and 90% less water than conventional farming methods. With a mission to 'revolutionize agriculture, ensuring accessibility to fresh, sustainable, locally grown produce and nourishing communities everywhere for generations to come,' Local Bounti's food is fresher, more nutritious, and lasts longer than traditional agriculture. To find out more, visit localbounti.com or follow Local Bounti on LinkedIn for the latest news and developments.

**Non-GAAP Financial Information**


This press release contains references to adjusted EBITDA, adjusted gross profit, adjusted gross margin percentage, and adjusted general and administrative expense, which are adjusted from results based on generally accepted accounting principles in the United States ("GAAP") and exclude certain expenses, gains, and losses. The Company defines and calculates adjusted EBITDA as net loss before the impact of interest expense, depreciation, and amortization, and adjusted to exclude stock-based compensation expense, change in fair value of warrant liability, the Cyclospora cost impact, and certain other non-core items, including business acquisition and strategic transaction due diligence and integration costs, litigation and other charges, and restructuring and business realignment costs, as itemized in the reconciliation. The Company defines and calculates adjusted gross profit as gross (loss) profit excluding depreciation, stock-based compensation, the Cyclospora cost impact, and certain other non-core items. The Cyclospora cost impact represents the Company's estimate of product waste costs incurred in the third quarter of 2026 in excess of typical waste levels as a result of the Cyclospora outbreak, excluding depreciation, and does not include any lost sales or revenue. The Company defines and calculates adjusted gross margin percentage as adjusted gross profit as a percent of sales. The Company defines and calculates adjusted general and administrative expense as general and administrative expense excluding stock-based compensation, depreciation, amortization, and certain other non-core items.


These non-GAAP financial measures are provided to enhance the user's understanding of the Company's prospects for the future and the historical performance for the context of the investor. The Company's management team uses these non-GAAP financial measures to assess performance and planning and forecasting future periods. These non-GAAP financial measures are not computed according to GAAP, and the methods the Company uses to compute them may differ from those used by other companies. Non-GAAP financial measures are supplemental; they should not be considered a substitute for, or superior to, financial information presented in accordance with GAAP and should be read only in conjunction with the Company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP.
